title: Design System: LegalOS Marketing
scope: marketing/ — the standalone dark landing page. Not the product app at web/, which is light-mode Astryx.

ink-3.displayName: Ink Tertiary (4.7:1 on ground — the contrast floor)

display.purpose: The H1 only. Sora 600, capped at 17ch above 860px, text-wrap: balance.

headline.purpose: Every section h2. Security section overrides down to clamp(1.9rem, 3vw, 2.7rem) because it sits inside a pane.

lede.purpose: Section-opening paragraph, --ink-2, max 62ch. Hero lede overrides to 56ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase section label with an 18x1px lead rule. Names the section's place in the product, never restates the heading. Deliberately neutral — it wore brass once and cost the citation seal its meaning.

statute.purpose: Arabic statute and document body — the naskh style Egyptian legal text is actually set in. Carries unicode-bidi: isolate but NOT direction: rtl.

arabic-ui.purpose: Arabic UI labels, matter names, chips and citation seals, so Arabic sits beside Manrope without a jolt.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover state for interactive panes (.pane--action), and any pane that must detach slightly at rest.

shadows.name: deep
shadows.purpose: Product surfaces (.ui) and the lightbox frame. Makes a screenshot read as an object on the page rather than an inset panel.

shadows.name: solid-button-seat
shadows.purpose: Primary button at rest. The inset white line is a top bevel, not a glow.

shadows.name: solid-button-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover — the ambient half turns violet.

shadows.name: violet-button-glow
shadows.purpose: Violet CTA at rest; hover extends to 0 16px 40px -10px rgba(109,91,255,1).

shadows.name: ui-top-highlight
shadows.purpose: Lit top edge inside a product surface, painted by .ui::after.

shadows.name: pane-lit-edge
shadows.value: linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), rgba(255,255,255,0) 42%) masked into a 1px ring via mask-composite: exclude
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow — the glass pane's lit top edge. Every .pane carries it on ::before.

shadows.name: field
shadows.value: radial-gradient(closest-side, …), filter: blur(90px), opacity 0.4–0.8, sized in vw/rem
shadows.purpose: Navy/violet atmosphere. A region behind a whole section, never an edge on a component.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out. The page's single motion curve: reveals, hovers, tab indicators, nav condense, accordion, lightbox.

motion.name: ease-soft
motion.purpose: Used for exactly one thing — the CTA sheen sweep. Do not introduce a third curve.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Stat count-up in JS, the numeric mirror of the CSS curve.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0.85s var(--ease), transform 0.95s var(--ease); from translateY(22px)
motion.purpose: The page's only reveal gesture. Staggered by an inline --reveal-delay in 70–90ms steps.

motion.name: reveal-observer
motion.purpose: Reveal trigger. Unobserves after firing; will-change released on transitionend.

motion.name: ambient-cycle
motion.purpose: Three-scene hero loop: matter board breathing, clause resolving to its article of law, timeline drawing. Masked to the open right region, off below 680px and under reduced motion, paused off-screen by IntersectionObserver.

motion.name: nav-condense
motion.value: transform 0.5s var(--ease), opacity 0.45s var(--ease); plate scaleY(62/76), row translate3d(0,-7px,0)
motion.purpose: Condense without touching height, so --nav-h and scroll-padding-top stay in agreement. Transform + opacity only, rAF-throttled.

motion.name: accordion
motion.value: grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr over 0.6s var(--ease); visibility 0s linear 0.6s on close
motion.purpose: Feature panels below 900px. The delayed visibility keeps collapsing content out of the tab order mid-animation.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Firm logo track, duplicated in JS for a seamless loop. Pauses on hover and focus-within; under reduced motion it becomes a plain scroller.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration / transition-duration: 0.001ms !important; reveals forced visible; ambient loop, weave, sheen and eyebrow pulse removed rather than frozen
motion.purpose: The hero swaps to its static poster frame, exactly as a paused film would look.

breakpoints.name: nav-links
breakpoints.note: Primary nav links hide; testimonial re-grids; integrations 8 → 6 columns.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.note: Every two-column section grid collapses; footer stacks; .ui-report stacks.

breakpoints.name: accordion
breakpoints.note: JS-driven via data-accordion-below on .feat, not a CSS media query — the swap also rewrites roles and aria-*.

breakpoints.name: burger
breakpoints.note: Burger appears; testimonial, stats and every .ui internal split go single-column; the .ui rail hides.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.note: --nav-h: 66px; ambient loop removed and the poster becomes the hero background; mockup tilt off; .ui surfaces shed columns rather than shrink type.

breakpoints.name: tabs-compact
breakpoints.note: Overview tab bar goes full-width and drops its icons.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.note: Integration grid held at 4 columns; pull-quote fixed at 1.15rem.

layout.shellWide: 1400px — nav, hero stage, testimonial, final CTA
layout.measures: headings 46rem; lede 62ch (hero 56ch); body 68ch; hero H1 17ch; mission statement 24ch; CTA heading 15ch
layout.gridRatios: overview 0.82/1.18 · features 0.86/1.14 · showcase 0.88/1.12 · security 1.05/0.95 · case study 1/1.08 · solutions 1.28/0.72 · testimonial 15rem/1fr/15.5rem
layout.bleedingRail: padding-inline: max(var(--shell-pad), (100% - var(--shell)) / 2 + var(--shell-pad)) — lets the insights carousel bleed to both viewport edges while its first card still aligns with the section heading

components.name: Glass Pane
components.description: The one glass recipe: 1px light border, low-alpha white fill, real backdrop blur, and a masked pseudo-element giving a lit top edge. Interactive panes brighten the border on hover rather than changing fill.

Smart Intake

A new enquiry arrives as a form, a WhatsApp message or a phone note and leaves as a matter.

narrative.overview:
A legal instrument is a document that carries its own proof — a seal, an article number, a signature that resolves to an authority. The page is built as one: a near-black room with weather in it, glass sheets holding real product surfaces, and a single brass mark that appears only where something on screen can be traced back to Egyptian statute. Nothing decorative is allowed to wear the seal. That restriction is the whole design; every other decision exists to keep it legible.

The density is editorial, not brochure. Sections breathe at clamp(6rem, 11vw, 11rem), copy is capped at 46rem for headings and 62–68ch for prose, and the visual weight lives in the product surfaces rather than in decoration. There is no stock photography, no icon-tile feature grid, and no raster screenshot anywhere on the page — every product screen is real markup. Colour is spent sparingly against a monochrome ground: violet is atmosphere and system state, brass is verification, and green/amber/red appear only inside product surfaces where they carry data meaning.

Motion is one authored idea repeated: a citation resolving. The hero's ambient loop draws an Arabic clause, underlines it in brass, then lands the article reference beneath it; the document panels hold the same moment statically. Everything else is arrival, not performance — a single fade-up on one easing curve, and a nav that condenses without animating layout.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#08090B) with all surfaces as low-alpha white overlays, never separate hexes
Navy→violet fields: blurred radial regions sized in viewport units, sitting behind whole sections
Brass as a functional, earned accent — never an eyebrow, tick, or icon tile
Four self-hosted faces (~167 KB), Arabic among them as product data rather than as a fallback
Real markup product screenshots that scale from one font-size
One glass recipe, one motion curve, one grain overlay
Content visible without JavaScript; every enhancement is additive

rules.name: The Seal Rule
rules.body: Brass marks only material that resolves to a source. If a new element cannot be traced to an article of law or a verifiable figure, it is --ink-2, --ink-3, or --violet-lit. The audit test: count the brass elements in a viewport; if any of them is a decoration, a tick, an eyebrow or an icon tile, the rule is broken.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Navy and violet are regions, never edges. A field is position: absolute, border-radius: 50%, filter: blur(90px), opacity 0.4–0.8, sized in vw/rem, and lives behind a whole section. Do not use either colour as a 1px border, a divider or a small fill outside the product surfaces.

rules.name: The Overlay Rule
rules.body: New surfaces are white at low alpha, not new dark hexes. Anything that needs to sit over a field must be translucent or it will read as a hole.

rules.name: The Isolate-Don't-Flip Rule
rules.body: .ar and .ar-doc carry unicode-bidi: isolate but deliberately NOT direction: rtl. The bidi algorithm already runs the Arabic right-to-left inside its own box; the box keeps the alignment of the row it sits in, so an Arabic matter title in an LTR table starts where its English subtitle starts. Surfaces that are genuinely right-to-left declare dir="rtl" on the container and inherit the real thing.

rules.name: The Optical Size Rule
rules.body: Arabic set inline in English copy is scaled up and loosened: .ar at 1.06em, .ar-doc at 1.08em with line-height: 2. Naskh at Manrope's optical size looks broken; do not normalise them to 1em.

rules.name: The Lit-Edge Rule
rules.body: One glass recipe, everywhere: 1px solid --hairline, background --surface-1, backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(140%), radius 28px, plus a masked ::before painting linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), transparent 42%) into a 1px ring via mask-composite: exclude. The blur is real and load-bearing — panes sit over violet fields and are supposed to pick them up.

rules.name: The Brighter-Not-Denser Rule
rules.body: Interactive panes hover by lifting 4px and brightening the border (--hairline → --hairline-strong) plus adding the lift shadow. The fill never changes. The glass reads as catching more light, not as changing material.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: A fixed full-page .grain overlay sits at z-index 1, opacity 0.035, mix-blend-mode: overlay, from an inline SVG feTurbulence. It exists because the large dark gradients band on 8-bit displays. Never remove it when adding a new full-width gradient; never raise it above ~0.04.

rules.name: The One Curve Rule
rules.body: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — exponential ease-out — is the page's motion curve. It drives reveals, hovers, tab indicators, the nav condense, the accordion, the lightbox, and (as 1 - 2^(-10t)) the stat count-up. --ease-soft exists for exactly one thing: the CTA sheen. Do not introduce a third.

dos: Do keep brass for material that resolves to a source. New elements default to --ink-2 / --ink-3 for neutral chrome and --violet-lit for system state.
Do build new surfaces as white-at-alpha overlays (--surface-1/2/3) so they pick up whatever field they cross.
Do express every interior measurement inside .ui in em. The whole product-surface system is one font-size away from being resizable; a single px value breaks that.

Do give any new section its atmosphere with a .field — absolutely positioned, blur(90px), sized in vw/rem, behind the content, with the section set to overflow: clip and its .shell raised to z-index: 1.
Do ship content visible and let script add the hiding class. Any new progressive-enhancement flag follows the js-boot pattern: set inline in <head>, removed at the end of init().
Do declare dir="rtl" on a container when a surface is genuinely right-to-left, and use .ar / .ar-doc for Arabic set inline in LTR rows.

Do use logical properties (margin-inline-start, border-inline-end, padding-inline, text-align: start) — the page already does throughout, which is what lets dir="rtl" surfaces work without a mirrored stylesheet.
Do colour status by meaning, not by arithmetic sign.
Do let a missing asset reveal an authored fallback (the ambient loop, the nameplate, the lightbox panel) rather than a broken element.
donts: Don't put brass on eyebrows, ticks, icon tiles, headings or hover states. That was tried; it cost the citation seal its meaning and was reverted.
Don't add direction: rtl to .ar or .ar-doc. unicode-bidi: isolate alone is the rule, so Arabic keeps the alignment of the row it sits in.
Don't use navy or violet as a border, divider or small fill in page chrome. They are fields.
Don't introduce a new dark hex for a surface. If it needs to be darker, it needs less alpha or more blur.
Don't change a pane's fill on hover — brighten its border.
Don't add a third easing curve, or a second reveal gesture. One fade-up, one curve.
Don't animate layout properties on scroll. The nav's condense is transform + opacity precisely so --nav-h and scroll-padding-top stay in agreement.
Don't remove the :not(.field) in .testimonial > *:not(.field); it keeps the absolutely-positioned glow out of the grid.
Don't let the citation seal clip. white-space: normal on .cite is load-bearing.
Don't fake a success state. The newsletter refuses rather than confirming an unrecorded subscription; hold that line for any form added here.
Don't introduce raster screenshots. Every product surface on this page is markup, and the page's credibility rests on it staying that way.
Don't carry these tokens into web/. That app is light-mode Astryx with an emerald/navy palette and Inter; this world stops at marketing/.
